note: Code read: after the step's approval exists the service re-reads the plugin records and declines the approval, then refuses with PLUGIN_OWNED, unless that install plan's record is still installing or installed and lists the skill. A completed uninstall therefore cannot be crossed by a late activation.

Code read: every store change marks the holds unavailable (the policy engine then denies every group a plugin could hold) and a failed read is retried in the background after 5 s, 15 s and then every minute until one lands.
Code read: the uninstall re-reads the connector scope under the plugin-record lock and throws a Conflict (scope changed, replan) if another plugin's install changed who keeps a connector.

Code read: both the mail and the calendar effects ask for the exact completed receipt first (`await completed() ? { replayed: true } : ...`) and only dispatch when none exists, so drift in the connection cannot hide a completed send nor cause a second one.
Code read: a JSON or SSE reply settles the call only when `isReplyFor` matches the request id and has no `method`; otherwise the call fails with 'did not include the expected JSON-RPC response'.
Code read: the execute paths call requireCodeModeEnabled('executing') at run time, so a legacy pending run is blocked by the live flag; terminal records are read through separate paths.
Code read: a 404 after a tools/call was sent now throws 'outcome is unknown' instead of reconnecting and re-posting; mcp-runtime.ts marks it manualReconciliationRequired.
Code read: recovery of a draft that is no longer an unlinked fence returns not_interrupted with the current draft and records nothing; the fence update is guarded by expectedUnlinkedUpdatedAt.

Code read: the approval is linked to the exact draft fence inside the approval-creation transaction; a stale fence throws StaleMailSendFenceError, which aborts that creation and returns the current draft.
Code read: the explicit check and the installs lookup ask Skill Hub for the exact snapshot id (`snapshotIds: [snapshotId]`); only the ordinary list keeps the newest-100 limit.
Code read: the shared portable-segment check rejects < > : " | ? * and trailing dots or spaces, and the manifest answers PIECE_PATH_INVALID with the exact pieces[n].path field.
Code read: both the skill-switch and skill-install stores subscribe to Gateway access changes and caller-scope changes and clear their timers and state, so a new caller starts from canonical state.
Code read: the synthesized default guild rule denies when inboundAccessMode is allowlist and the sender list is empty; a saved explicit guild rule is used first.

Code read: a tool in a switched-off group stays in the inspectable catalog with the warning 'This tool group is switched off.' and is marked callable:false, so the frozen callable catalog excludes it.
Code read: the SMTP message takes args.bodyText untouched as `text`.
Code read: Tools and Chat now say uninstalling releases the holds and that, if the group stays off, the operator can switch it on.

Code read: the offset write carries the connection revision and a TelegramPollRevisionChangedError is not counted as a head failure, so stale poll work cannot admit an event or drop an update after the cutover.

Live (check only, nothing installed): a folder plugin with two good skills and one skill without front matter shows 'This skill didn't pass GoatCitadel's checks.' and 'So it can't be installed.' It never says why or what to change. The Skills tab words each blocker; the plugin panel prints the Gateway's one fixed sentence.

finding.title: A plugin skill that fails its check says only that it failed, not why or what to fix
finding.trigger: Capabilities › Plugins › Add from folder with a plugin whose skill has no front matter; press Check.
finding.expected: The line names the reason (for example 'its SKILL.md has no name') and the fix, as the Skills tab does for a skill checked on its own.
finding.actual: The row reads 'This skill didn't pass GoatCitadel's checks.' and the panel ends 'So it can't be installed.' The blocker code is only in Technical details.

note: A plugin with a skill that fails its check cannot be installed at all (the panel says 'So it can't be installed'), so an installed plugin never holds blocked skills, and the list note is only the piece counts ('2 skills, 1 connector'), not a usable-of-total figure. Live: the mixed plugin shows two 'Passed' rows and one failed row and no combined count.

A manifest with an empty name is refused, and the panel then leaves out the 'What it is' block and uses 'this plugin' in its sentences instead of a blank. Live: the nameless folder plugin opens a panel titled 'Install a plugin' with one refusal line and 'So it can't be installed.', no empty heading or quotes. (The refusal sentence does not name the empty field: the same canned-copy pattern as OL-35.)

'So it can't be installed.' is one fixed line placed right after the reason: under the pieces list for a blocked piece, under the refusal sentence for a refused manifest. Live, both cases showed it once, in that place, with no layout jump.

A Claude Code skill folder named like a generated id now gets a fallback id, so that collision no longer happens. A manifest with two pieces sharing an id is still refused with 'Two of its pieces have the same id.': it names neither the id nor the pieces, though the Gateway's own sentence does (contracts plugins.ts:269).

finding.title: A plugin with a repeated piece id is refused without saying which id
finding.trigger: Capabilities › Plugins › Add from folder with a manifest whose two pieces both have id skill-2; press Check.
finding.expected: The refusal names the id (skill-2) and says to give each piece its own id.
finding.actual: The panel says 'Two of its pieces have the same id.' and 'So it can't be installed.' The Gateway's sentence with the id is replaced by the screen's canned line.
